title: Bucks 128–127 Pacers in Overtime: Herro and Siakam's Scoring Explained
description: Milwaukee's October 16 preseason win, explained through Tyler Herro's 25 points and Pascal Siakam's 24, with a clear scoring breakdown.

sections.heading: The result
paragraphs: Milwaukee beat Indiana 128–127 in overtime on October 16, 2026. This was a preseason game. Tyler Herro scored 25 points for the Bucks and Pascal Siakam 24 for the Pacers. Their scoring lines offer a simple way to understand the box score.

sections.heading: One point apart, different routes
paragraphs: Herro made 10 of 16 field-goal attempts, including 5 of 7 three-pointers, and had no free-throw attempts. Siakam made 8 of 10 field-goal attempts, also hit 5 of 7 threes, and converted all 3 free throws. The chart separates the points produced by each scoring type.
bullets: Herro: five two-point baskets produced 10 points; five threes produced 15; free throws added 0. Total: 25.
Siakam: three two-point baskets produced 6 points; five threes produced 15; free throws added 3. Total: 24.

sections.heading: How field goals become points
paragraphs: In a basketball box score, field goals include both two-point and three-point baskets. To find made two-pointers, subtract made threes from total made field goals. Then multiply the two-point baskets by two, the threes by three, and add made free throws. That is why the chart uses points on its axis, rather than the number of successful shots.

sections.heading: What the comparison tells us
paragraphs: Both players supplied 15 points from beyond the arc. Herro's two-point baskets added four more points than Siakam's, while Siakam added three at the free-throw line. That accounts for the one-point difference between their personal totals. It does not explain Milwaukee's one-point victory: every other player's scoring and the order of the possessions also belong to the game.

sections.heading: Efficiency is one piece of the picture
paragraphs: Siakam's 8-for-10 shooting works out to 80%, and Herro's 10-for-16 to 62.5%. Those percentages describe this game's field-goal attempts. They do not measure the difficulty of each shot, defensive contribution, or everything a player created for teammates. A better shooting percentage and more total points answer different questions.

sections.heading: What to look for in the replay
paragraphs: Use the official highlights to put actions around the numbers: was a basket created off a pass, a dribble, or a second opportunity after a miss? Follow the player who starts the move as well as the player who finishes it.

sections.heading: The regular-season reset
paragraphs: The NBA schedule lists Milwaukee at Washington and Indiana at New Orleans on October 21 for their regular-season openers. Herro's and Siakam's shooting in this preseason meeting gives viewers specific performances to revisit as the new season begins.
